question: You've seen this screen. Why does every AI-built app look the same?

hook_visual.intent: three fabricated app screens that are the same screen with different words

points.claim: unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that finds the slop in a screen and names it, with where it lives, before it edits anything.
points.spoken: unslop is a skill for Claude Code or Codex, and it starts by naming the slop out loud, and where it lives.
points.source_note: README: 'unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface' + 'Audit. Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.'

visual.intent: the slop named where it lives, on the screen itself

points.title: FIRST, IT NAMES THE SLOP
points.sub: It says where each sign lives.

points.claim: It proposes a direction taken from the product — character, the moment that carries the colour, a signature detail — and you steer it before it edits anything.
points.spoken: Then it asks what your product actually is. Your answer becomes the direction: the character, the one moment that carries the color, the signature detail.
points.source_note: README: 'It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early.' + 'Direction. Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.'

visual.intent: the direction typed from your answer: character, one moment, a detail

points.title: YOUR ANSWER IS THE DIRECTION

points.claim: It then fixes the screen in nine passes — spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion — in that order, on the same screen.
points.spoken: Then it redraws the same screen in nine passes, so what you get back still looks like your product, just designed.
points.source_note: README: 'Passes. Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.'

visual.intent: the same screen changing pass by pass

points.title: NINE PASSES, ONE SCREEN

points.claim: You run it by typing /unslop with your screen or a live link, and it works in whatever the screen is built with.
points.spoken: Type unslop, then your screen or a live link. It runs in Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte or plain CSS.
points.source_note: README: 'In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want.' + 'It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS … even on a live site when all you have is a link.'

visual.intent: typing the slash command, then the stacks it runs in

points.title: TYPE SLASH UNSLOP
points.sub: A screen, or a live link.

points.claim: The result keeps the layout and the words of the screen it was given; what changes is the product it now looks like.
points.spoken: Same layout, same words, different product. That is the whole point.
points.source_note: README: 'shows your product instead of a glossy blob' + 'fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review' — the screen is fixed, not replaced.

visual.intent: a dragged before/after of the same layout and words

points.title: SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT PRODUCT

catch: If your screen is already good it says so; it asks before any paid image; and it needs Claude Code or Codex to run.
catch_sub: An agent skill: it works where your agent works.

catch_visual.intent: what to expect: it says so when the screen is already good, it asks before any paid image

cover.visual: one vibecoded screen on the left, the same screen redesigned on the right, divider dragged between them

media.design: Paper plate split down the middle: the same fabricated app screen twice — violet gradient with a glow and emoji badges on the left, the redesigned paper version on the right — with the headline sitting across the divider.
A fabricated browser window on the paper plate, half slop and half redesigned, with the audit labels (gradient, glow, emoji) pinned to the slop half and a single violet accent on the clean half.

Full-bleed paper with the nine pass chips (spacing, colour, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion) stacked as a vertical rail, the last three lit violet, and a small before/after screen in the corner.

cta: Comment UNSLOP and I'll pin the repo.
